study_id: Johnston et al. - 2025 - Estimating Calibrated Risks Using Focal Loss and Gradient-Boosted Trees for Clinical Risk Prediction

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study uses gradient‑boosted decision trees (a non‑linear AI model) to predict post‑lung transplant cancer risk in adult recipients, includes relevant outcomes, and is a peer‑reviewed article published after 2018.

identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective analysis of SRTR lung transplant and BRFSS diabetes datasets using calibrated focal-loss GBDT models.
identification_methods.Author_name: Henry Johnston; Nandini Nair; Dongping Du
identification_methods.Institution: Department of Industrial, Manufacturing, and Systems Engineering, Texas Tech University; Heart and Vascular Institute, Pennsylvania State University College of Medicine
identification_methods.Address: Lubbock, TX 79409, USA; Hershey, PA 17033, USA
identification_methods.Dataset Source: Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients (SRTR); Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS)
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included lung transplant recipients ≥18 years, excluded retransplantation, missing follow‑up, and unknown cancer status; diabetes cohort from 2015 BRFSS survey.
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: Gradient‑Boosted Decision Trees (XGBoost, LightGBM) with focal loss and Ψγ calibration
identification_methods.Comparator: Standard XGBoost with cross‑entropy loss; logistic regression (unregularized, LASSO, ridge); Platt scaling and isotonic regression calibrations
identification_methods.Input Variables: 54 features including demographics, immunosuppression, viral infections, HLA types for lung transplant; 21 survey variables for diabetes
identification_methods.Missing Data Handling: Median imputation for numeric features and mode imputation for categorical features
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Bayesian hyperparameter tuning of GBDT; Ψγ closed‑form transformation for calibration; decision‑threshold optimization to maximize balanced accuracy

population.Inclusion criteria: Lung transplant recipients from SRTR, age ≥18 years
population.Exclusion criteria: Retransplantation, patients under 18 years, without follow-up records, unknown cancer status
population.Population Notes: Dataset split into 70% training and 30% testing sets

interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: Tabular clinical variables (demographics, medical history, transplant data, survey responses)
interventions_outcomes.Number of Predictors: 54 features for PTLD prediction; 21 features for diabetes prediction
interventions_outcomes.Temporal Handling: Static baseline data (risk prediction at fixed time horizons)
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Bayesian hyperparameter optimization to select focal loss parameter; Ψγ transformation applied to calibrate confidence scores of GBDT trained with focal loss
interventions_outcomes.Reported outcomes in study: Post‑transplant cancer risk (PTLD) at 1, 3, 5, 8 and 10 years; diabetes status prediction
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Metrics include AUROC, H‑measure, average precision, Brier score, calibration slope and intercept; balanced accuracy evaluated with prevalence‑based threshold
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: Calibrated focal‑aware XGBoost achieved AUROC 0.700, Brier score 0.128 and calibration slope 0.968 for 10‑year cancer risk, improving calibration while preserving discrimination
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reported against: Standard XGBoost trained with cross‑entropy loss
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reported as: AUROC, Brier score and calibration slope
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reference arm: Standard XGBoost AUROC 0.736 for 10‑year cancer risk
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: Lung transplant recipients in the SRTR dataset
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: AUROC on a completely held‑out test cohort; Brier score as overall accuracy metric
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: Calibration improved markedly after Ψγ transformation while AUROC remained unchanged
